record.paper_title: Open problems on graph eigenvalues studied with AutoGraphiX
record.original_question: For each integer n at least 10, is the connected n-vertex graph with maximum irregularity always a pineapple graph PA(n,q), where a pineapple graph consists of a q-vertex clique together with an independent set on the remaining n−q vertices such that every vertex of the independent set is adjacent to one and the same clique vertex, and where the conjectured optimal clique size is q = ceil(n/2) + 1? Equivalently, does this specific pineapple maximize λ1(G) − d̄(G) over all connected graphs G on n vertices, where λ1(G) is the largest adjacency eigenvalue and d̄(G) is the average degree?

evidence.quote: The next section discusses the problem related to the irregularity of a graph... The following conjecture related to the irregularity of a graph have been formulated after some experiments with the system AGX.
Conjecture 2.1... The most irregular connected graph on n (n ≥ 10) vertices is a pineapple PA(n,q) in which the clique size q is equal to ⌈n/2⌉ +1.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For an integer $n \geq 10$ and an integer $q$ with $1 \leq q \leq n$, define the pineapple graph $PA(n,q)$ as the graph on $n$ vertices obtained from a clique $K_q$ on $q$ vertices together with an independent set $I$ on the remaining $n-q$ vertices, by joining every vertex of $I$ to one fixed (common) vertex of the clique. For a simple connected graph $G$ on $n$ vertices, let $\lambda_1(G)$ denote the largest eigenvalue of the adjacency matrix of $G$, and let $\bar d(G) = \frac{2|E(G)|}{n}$ denote the average degree. Define the irregularity of $G$ as $\varepsilon(G) = \lambda_1(G) - \bar d(G)$.

Prove or disprove: for every integer $n \geq 10$, the unique connected graph on $n$ vertices that maximizes $\varepsilon(G)$ is the pineapple graph $PA(n,q)$ with $q = \lceil n/2 \rceil + 1$.
artifact.status_search_result: Tait and Tobin (2016, "Three conjectures in extremal spectral graph theory", arXiv:1606.01916) proved the conjecture of Aouchiche et al. that for sufficiently large $n$, the unique connected $n$-vertex graph maximizing $\lambda_1(G) - \bar d(G)$ is the pineapple graph $PA(n, \lceil n/2\rceil + 1)$.

status_evidence.title: Three conjectures in extremal spectral graph theory
status_evidence.snippet: Tait and Tobin prove three conjectures including that the pineapple graph maximizes the irregularity measure λ1(G) − d̄(G) among connected n-vertex graphs for sufficiently large n.
status_evidence.claim: The pineapple conjecture was proved by Tait and Tobin (for n large enough).

status_evidence.title: Eight theorems in extremal spectral graph theory (Tait survey)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey notes that the conjecture of Aouchiche et al. that the pineapple PA(n, ⌈n/2⌉+1) maximizes λ1 − d̄ over connected n-vertex graphs was proved by Tait–Tobin.
status_evidence.claim: The maximum-irregularity pineapple conjecture is established as a theorem.
